title: A simple type scale
summary: Headings and body text sized in rem, with weights and line heights to match.
explanation: A type scale is a short list of sizes you reuse everywhere, so the page has a clear hierarchy instead of a dozen slightly different sizes. Here each step is about 1.25× the one below.
rem is relative to the root font size (16px unless the reader changed it), so the whole scale grows if someone sets a larger default in their browser. px would ignore that setting.
Big text needs a tighter line-height than body text; and a semi-bold 600 often looks better on headings than the default bold.
tryThis: Change the h1 to 3rem: the hierarchy gets more dramatic.
Set font-weight: 400 on .title: the heading only stands out by size now.
Give .title line-height: 1.6 like the body: big text with loose lines looks disconnected.

children.text: Body text at the base size. Every other size is a step up or down from here, which keeps the page consistent.
